findings: Across 108 synthetic full-call conditions, the fitted log-log scaling exponent for MAE versus accumulated terms was 0.36413.
The one-variable power-law fit achieved log-log R2 = 0.95262.
Mean MAE increased from 0.00168 at 1 accumulated term to 0.04449 at 6272 accumulated terms.
At 32 input channels, increasing Fourier components from 4 to 8 increased mean MAE from 0.00722 to 0.01039.
At 784 input channels, increasing Fourier components from 1 to 8 increased mean MAE from 0.01600 to 0.04449.
interpretation: Within this synthetic Q.ANT CPU-backend experiment, accumulated-term count is a strong descriptive predictor of reference-to-backend numerical error. This motivates an architecture intervention that reduces the fan-in seen by each Q.ANT KAN call. The exponent is empirical for the tested random parameter distribution and is not a universal Q.ANT or photonic scaling law.
next_research_direction: Compare a monolithic FashionMNIST QFourier classifier with grouped low-fan-in QFourier classifiers that preserve the same Fourier grid while partitioning the 784 input pixels across multiple Q.ANT calls, then combine group logits additively.
limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
Synthetic amplitudes and phases differ from learned FashionMNIST parameters.
The power-law fit is descriptive over the tested range and should not be extrapolated beyond it without validation.
